name: Optical-fiber communication links
summary: In the mid-1970s links sending telephone, data and television signals as light through glass fibres went into practical service in Japan, the US and Britain.
description: An optical transmitter modulates light sent through a guided optical fiber to a detector, carrying voice or data between endpoints.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.

events.statement: Fujitsu reports delivering 32-Mb/s optical transmission equipment to the Japanese telephone organization in 1974.
events.scope: Fujitsu 32-Mb/s optical-fiber transmission equipment delivered to the organization it calls NTT.
events.population: Fujitsu and the Japanese telephone organization
events.caveats: The source does not establish paid sale, operational service, or first independent use. The recipient is described using the later familiar name NTT.

evidence.supports: Fujitsu dates delivery of the equipment to 1974.

date.basis: Latest supported use or availability; the first worldwide entry is not established.

events.statement: A fiber link restored the Dorset police computer-to-terminal connection in 1975 after lightning damage.
events.scope: Optical-fiber link joining the police computer and command-room video terminals.
events.caveats: The reported mid-September operation and fall installation may reflect differing date conventions; the exact first use day and any world-first claim remain unresolved.

evidence.supports: The historical account says police resumed operation after the installation in September 1975.
The 1976 article describes data transfer to police supervising inspectors.
The later article places installation in fall 1975.

date.label: by 1975
date.basis: Latest supported use or availability; the first worldwide entry is not established.

events.statement: The USS Little Rock fiber-optic telephone system had entered operation by 1975, inferred from a 1976 report that it was in its third year.
events.scope: Shipboard fiber telephone with optical sources, receivers and pulse-position-modulated voice.
events.caveats: Electronic Design reports six stations, but a contemporaneous U.S. Naval Institute account says five; the count or system may have changed. Installation is dated 1973 in the NASA report; the exact operating start and call records are not documented. The 1976 article separately captions a Corning cable but does not attribute its attenuation to the ship. Prior guided-light demonstrations and imaging fibers predate this service.

evidence.supports: The April 1976 article says a fiber-optic telephone reported as six-station was in its third year of operation aboard USS Little Rock.
The NASA contractor report dates installation of a shipboard secure telephone to 1973.
The chapter distinguishes earlier imaging fibers from a 1965 optical data-link demonstration.
The Navy Institute account describes five stations, differing from the April report’s six.

events.statement: Rediffusion began using a glass-fiber television trunk cable in the Hastings area in March 1976.
events.population: Rediffusion television network operators and subscribers
events.caveats: The source describes a trunk route serving a broader television system; it does not establish a direct fiber connection to each subscriber.

evidence.supports: The contemporary IEEE account dates Rediffusion use to March 1976.
